title: Provisioning: add state machine types + persistence (with migration + backwards compat)
author: Gabe Wilson
release_notes: - Control plane now persists Dedicated pool provisioning runs and stage transitions in a first-class model. - Adds new enum states and transition validation for Requested→Provisioning→Imaging→Bootstrapping→Validating→Ready/Failed. - Introduces DB migration with backwards-compatible reads; legacy pool registration flows continue to function.
body: Context: As part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint we need a durable, auditable state machine for Dedicated pool bring-up that can survive retries, operator intervention, and service restarts. Today the control plane tracks some of this implicitly (logs + ad-hoc fields on pool records), which makes it hard to reason about "where" a pool is in the bring-up pipeline, and it makes stage timing metrics brittle. This PR introduces the typed state machine + persistence layer changes that other PRs will build on (orchestration runner, stage timing events, readiness gates). Changes: (1) Adds new domain types for provisioning runs, stage states, terminal outcomes, and validated transition rules. (2) Adds persistence models + DB schema for provisioning runs and transitions, including an append-only transition log for auditability. (3) Updates control-plane read/write paths to support dual operation: legacy Dedicated pool registration continues to work; new provisioning runs can be created and progressed without requiring routing changes yet. (4) Adds migration and compatibility behavior: older control plane versions ignore the new tables; newer versions can read legacy pool state and "synthesize" a minimal provisioning run view when no run exists, to avoid breaking UI/API consumers during rollout. Migration notes: This PR adds a forward-only Postgres migration creating tables dedicated_pool_provisioning_runs and dedicated_pool_provisioning_transitions plus indexes for pool_id and correlation_id. The migration does not modify existing pool tables. New code paths are gated so that in prod we can deploy the schema first, then the service code, then enable creation of runs behind a feature flag in a follow-up PR. Backwards compatibility: (a) Existing pool registration endpoints remain unchanged. (b) Any unknown state values returned from persistence are treated as "Failed" with reason "unknown_state" and surfaced to operators as a safe default; this is defensive in case of partial deploys. (c) New API shapes are internal-only in this PR; externally visible pool status remains the existing field set. (d) Transition validation is enforced only for write paths that go through the new provisioning service methods; direct DB edits / manual remediation are still possible but will be audited as "manual" transitions when using the provided admin helper. Operational notes: Transitions include actor (service/principal) and optional message. This will be used later for Slack bot summaries and for time-to-ready stage histograms. Rollout plan: Apply migration in staging, deploy control plane, run a synthetic provisioning run through transitions via admin tool, verify queries + indexes, then proceed to wiring orchestration. Testing: unit tests for transition rules, repository CRUD, and migration smoke (schema existence).

illustrative_snippet: New states: Requested, Provisioning, Imaging, Bootstrapping, Validating, Ready, Failed. Transitions are append-only; repository enforces monotonic stage progress unless actor=admin and override_reason is provided. Reads from legacy pool status return a synthesized run only when provisioning_runs table has no entry for the pool_id.
conversation: Ethan Park (2025-02-21): Can we ensure we don't accidentally mark Ready without a canary later? I want the state machine to make "Ready" terminal and only reachable from Validating.

Gabe Wilson (2025-02-21): Yep — Ready is terminal and only reachable from Validating. Also added a guard that prevents any further transitions after Ready/Failed unless actor=admin + override_reason. Perf-canary gating will be enforced in the orchestration layer before it writes the Validating→Ready transition.
Rafael Mendes (2025-02-21): For partial rollouts, what's the behavior if the code deploys before the migration in a region? We’ve been burned by that ordering before.

Gabe Wilson (2025-02-21): Good call. Repository init does a schema presence check; if tables are missing it logs once and hard-disables provisioning run writes (feature flag forced off), while leaving legacy pool behavior intact. Added that note to migrations/README.md.
Benji Okafor (2025-02-22): Please include correlation_id now; we’ll need it for structured events (ENG-2748) and Slack updates (ENG-2758).
Gabe Wilson (2025-02-22): Added correlation_id to runs table and to the domain type + repository API. Index included.
Miles Thornton (2025-02-22): Multi-region: any risk of high-cardinality indexes if correlation_id is UUID per run? Also, do we have a retention plan for the transition log?

Gabe Wilson (2025-02-22): correlation_id index is btree and bounded by number of provisioning runs (not per request). Retention: not in this PR; proposing 90d retention + archive in a follow-up once we have metrics consumption. Added TODO and a comment in migration README.

Ethan Park (2025-02-23): Request changes: please rename "Provisioning" vs "Provisioned"—I've seen confusion in other docs. Also add explicit enum mapping to string values to avoid accidental reordering bugs.
Gabe Wilson (2025-02-23): Done — removed "Provisioned" entirely (only stage states), and enums are explicit string unions persisted as text. Updated tests accordingly.
Rafael Mendes (2025-02-24): LGTM once CI is green.

security_considerations: Transition log records actor_id and actor_type for auditability; admin overrides require override_reason and are tagged manual=true. No secrets stored. Access to admin helper remains restricted to control-plane admins.
